#### 3.4.23 Migrate data from a self-managed Db2 for LUW database to a PolarDB for MySQL instance

**Db2 for LUW database to a PolarDB for**

**MySQL instance**

This topic describes how to use Data Transmission Service (DTS) to migrate data from a Db2 for LUW database to a PolarDB for MySQL instance that uses local disks.

**Prerequisites**

You have created a source Db2 for LUW database and a destination PolarDB for MySQL instance that uses local disks. The available storage space of the destination database is larger than the size of the data to be migrated from the source database.

**Precautions**

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Source database limitations | Bandwidth requirements: The server that hosts the source database must have sufficient outbound bandwidth. Otherwise, the data migration speed is affected. The tables to be migrated must have primary keys or UNIQUE constraints, and the fields must be unique. Otherwise, duplicate data may exist in the destination database. The data capture property must be enabled for the tables to be migrated. If you migrate data at the table level and need to edit the migration objects, such as mapping table and column names, a single data migration task supports a maximum of 1,000 tables. If you exceed this limit, a request error is reported after you submit the task. In this case, split the tables into multiple migration tasks or configure a task to migrate the entire database. If you perform incremental migration, note the following requirements for data logs: Data logging must be enabled. Otherwise, an error is reported during the precheck, and the data migration task cannot start. For an incremental migration task, DTS requires that data logs in the source database are retained for more than 24 hours. For a task that includes both full migration and incremental migration, DTS requires that data logs in the source database are retained for at least 7 days. After the full migration is complete, you can change the log retention period to more than 24 hours. If the log retention period is shorter than required, the task may fail because DTS cannot obtain the data logs. In extreme cases, data inconsistency or data loss may occur. Issues that arise because the log retention period is shorter than required are not covered by the DTS Service-Level Agreement (SLA). Limitations on operations in the source database: During the full migration phase, do not perform DDL operations that change the database or table schema. Otherwise, the data migration task fails. If you perform only full data migration, do not write new data to the source instance. Otherwise, data inconsistency occurs between the source and destination databases. To ensure real-time data consistency, select both full data migration and incremental data migration. |

| Other limitations | A single data migration task can migrate only one database. To migrate multiple databases, you must configure a data migration task for each database. DTS uses the Change Data Capture (CDC) replication technology of Db2 for LUW to migrate incremental updates to the destination database. However, CDC replication has its own limitations. For more information, see Data type restrictions for SQL Replication. Before you migrate data, evaluate the performance of the source and destination databases. Migrate data during off-peak hours. Initial full data synchronization consumes read and write resources on both the source and destination databases, which may increase the database load. Initial full data synchronization runs concurrent INSERT operations, which causes table fragmentation in the destination database. As a result, the tablespace in the destination instance is larger than that in the source instance. If the data to be migrated contains content that requires 4-byte storage, such as uncommon characters or emojis, the destination database and tables that receive the data must use the utf8mb4 charset. Note If you use DTS to migrate the database and table schemas, you must set the character set server parameter at the instance level for the destination _ _ database to utf8mb4. During the DTS migration, if data is written to the destination database by sources other than DTS, data inconsistency may occur between the source and destination databases. |
|---|---|
| Special cases | Because the source Db2 for LUW database is a self-managed database, note the following: During migration, if a primary/standby switchover occurs in the source database, the migration task fails. The latency of DTS is calculated by comparing the timestamp of the last migrated data record with the current timestamp. If no DML operations are performed on the source database for a long time, the latency information may be inaccurate. If the displayed latency is too high, you can perform a DML operation on the source database to update the latency information. Note If you choose to migrate the entire database, you can also create a heartbeat table. The heartbeat table periodically updates or writes data every second. |

**SQL operations supported by incremental migration**

| Operation type | SQL operation |
|---|---|
| DML | INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE |

**Permission requirements for database accounts**

| Database | Full migration | Schema migration | Incremental migration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Db2 for LUW | CONNECT and SELECT permissions | CONNECT and SELECT permissions | DBADM permission |
| PolarDB for MySQL | Read and write permissions on the destination database. Important Use a privileged account. |   |   |

**Procedure**

1. Create a data migration instance.
When you create the instance, set **Source Database Type** to **DB2 LUW** and
**Destination Database Type** to **PolarDB for MySQL**.
2. On the Data Migration page, find the data migration instance that you created, and click
**Configure Task** in the Actions column.
3. Configure the source and destination databases.

| Category | Configuration | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Task Name | None | The task name that DTS automatically generates. We recommend that you specify a descriptive name that makes it easy to identify the task. You do not need to specify a unique task name. |
| Source Database Information | Database Type | Fixed as DB2 LUW. |
|   | Connection Type | Select Public IP. |
|   | Instance Region | The region of the source instance that you selected when you purchased the data migration instance. This parameter cannot be changed. |
|   | DNS Or IP Address | Enter the IP address of the server that hosts the self- managed Db2 for LUW database. |

|   | Port | Enter the service port of the self-managed Db2 for LUW database. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Database Name | Enter the name of the database to which the tables to be migrated belong. |
|   | Database Account | Enter the database account of the self-managed Db2 for LUW database. |
|   | Database Password | Enter the password for the database account. |
| Destination Database Information | Database Type | Select PolarDB for MySQL. |
|   | Connection Type | Select Cloud Instance. |
|   | Instance Region | The region of the destination instance that you selected when you purchased the data migration instance. This parameter cannot be changed. |
|   | Cross-account | Specifies whether to synchronize data across Alibaba Cloud accounts. In this example, No is selected. |
|   | Architecture Type | In this example, Local Disk Dual-node is selected. |
|   | PolarDB Instance ID | Select the ID of the destination PolarDB for MySQL instance. |
|   | Database Account | Enter the database account of the destination PolarDB for MySQL instance. |
|   | Database Password | Enter the password for the database account. |
|   | Connection Method | Select a method as needed. |

4. After you complete the configurations, click **Test Connection And Proceed** at the bottom
of the page. If your self-managed Db2 for LUW database uses a whitelist, add the IP addresses of the DTS servers to the database whitelist. The IP addresses are displayed in the dialog box that appears. After you add the IP addresses, click **Test**
**Connection And Proceed**.
If your self-managed Db2 for LUW database does not require a whitelist, click
**Test Connection And Proceed**.
5. Configure the task objects.

| Configu ration | Description |
|---|---|
| Task Steps | To perform only full migration, select Schema Migration and Full Migration. To perform migration without service interruption, select Schema Migration, Full Migration, and Incremental Migration. Note If you do not select Schema Migration, ensure that the destination database contains the databases and tables that will receive the data. If needed, you can use the table and column name mapping feature in the Selected Objects box. If you do not select Incremental Migration, do not write new data to the source instance during data migration to ensure data consistency. |
| Handlin g Of Existin g Tables In Destina tion | Precheck And Block: Checks whether a table with the same name exists in the destination database. If a table with the same name does not exist, the precheck passes. If a table with the same name exists, the precheck reports an error, and the data migration task does not start. Ignore And Continue: Skips the check for tables with the same name in the destination database. Warning If you select Ignore And Continue, data inconsistency may occur and pose risks to your business. For example: If the table schemas are consistent and a record in the destination database has the same primary key value as a record in the source database, the record in the destination database is retained. The record from the source database is not migrated. If the table schemas are inconsistent, only some columns of data may be migrated, or the migration may fail. |

| Case Sensiti vity Of Object Names In Destina tion Databa se | You can configure the case sensitivity policy for the names of databases, tables, and columns that are migrated to the destination instance. By default, DTS Default Policy is selected. You can also select a policy that is consistent with the default policy of the source or destination database. For more information, see Case sensitivity of object names in the destination database. |
|---|---|
| Source Databa se Objects | Select one or more objects from the Source Objects section and click the icon to add the objects to the Selected Objects section. Note You can expand the navigation tree and use regular expressions to search for objects. You can select migration objects at the schema or table level. |
| Selecte d Objects | By default, after an object is migrated to the destination database, the name of the object remains unchanged. You can use the object name mapping feature to change the names of the objects that are migrated to the destination database. For more information, see Object name mapping. Note To filter data using a WHERE clause, right-click the table to be migrated in the Selected Objects box and set the filter condition in the dialog box that appears. To select the SQL operations performed on a specific database or table, right-click an object in the Selected Objects section. In the dialog box that appears, select the SQL operations that you want to migrate. If you use the object name mapping feature to rename an object, other objects that are dependent on the object may fail to be migrated. |

6. Click **Next: Advanced Configuration** to configure advanced settings.

| Configuration Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Select Engine Type For Destination Database | If needed, you can set the engine type of the destination database to InnoDB or X-Engine. |

| Retry Time After Source/Destination Database Connection Failure | After the migration task starts, DTS reports an error if the connection to the source or destination database fails. DTS then automatically retries the connection. The default retry duration is 720 minutes. You can also specify a custom retry duration from 10 to 1,440 minutes. We recommend that you set the duration to more than 30 minutes. If DTS successfully reconnects to the source or destination database within the specified duration, the migration task automatically resumes. Otherwise, the migration task fails. Note If you have multiple DTS instances, such as DTS instance A and DTS instance B, for the same source or destination, and you set the network retry duration to 30 minutes for A and 60 minutes for B, the shorter duration of 30 minutes is used for both instances. |
|---|---|

7. In the lower part of the page, click **Next: Precheck and Start Task**.

**Important**

Before you can start the data migration task, DTS performs a precheck. You can start the data migration task only after the task passes the precheck. If the task fails to pass the precheck, click **View Details** next to each failed item. After you troubleshoot the issues based on the causes, run a precheck again.
8. Wait until **Success Rate** reaches 100%. Then, click **Back**.
If Incremental Data Migration is not selected, wait until the migration task is complete. If Incremental Data Migration is selected, the migration task does not automatically stop. In this case, you must wait until the migration task enters the **Running** state and is not delayed, and then manually stop the task.

#### 3.4.24 Migrate data from a self-managed Db2 for LUW database to a PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance

**Db2 for LUW database to a PolarDB for**

**PostgreSQL instance**

This topic describes how to use Data Transmission Service (DTS) to migrate data from a Db2 for LUW database to a PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance.

**Prerequisites**

You have created a source Db2 for LUW database and a destination PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance. The available storage space in the destination database is larger than the size of the data to be migrated. You have created a database in the destination PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance to store the migrated data.

**Notes**

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Source database limits | Bandwidth requirements: The server that hosts the source database must have sufficient outbound bandwidth. Insufficient bandwidth affects the data migration speed. Tables to be migrated must have primary keys or UNIQUE constraints, and the fields must be unique. Otherwise, duplicate data may be generated in the destination database. The data capture property must be enabled for the tables to be migrated. If you migrate objects at the table level and need to edit the objects, such as mapping table and column names, a single data migration task can migrate a maximum of 1,000 tables. If the number of tables exceeds this limit, an error is reported after you submit the task. In this case, split the tables into multiple migration tasks, or configure a task to migrate the entire database. If you perform incremental migration, for data logs: Data logs must be enabled. Otherwise, an error is reported during the precheck, and the data migration task cannot start. For an incremental migration task, DTS requires that data logs of the source database are retained for more than 24 hours. For a full and incremental migration task, DTS requires that data logs of the source database are retained for at least 7 days. After the full migration is complete, you can set the log retention period to more than 24 hours. Otherwise, the DTS task may fail because DTS cannot obtain the data logs. In extreme cases, data inconsistency or loss may occur. Issues that are caused by a log retention period shorter than the required period are not covered by the DTS Service-Level Agreement (SLA). Operation limits on the source database: During the full migration phase, do not perform DDL operations to change the database or table schemas. Otherwise, the data migration task fails. If you perform only full data migration, do not write new data to the source instance. Otherwise, data inconsistency between the source and destination instances occurs. To ensure real-time data consistency, select both Full Data Migration and Incremental Data Migration. |
| Other limits | A single data migration task can migrate only one database. To migrate multiple databases, configure a data migration task for each database. DTS uses the Change Data Capture (CDC) replication technology of Db2 for LUW to migrate incremental updates from the Db2 for LUW database to the destination database. However, CDC replication has its own limitations. For more information, see Data type restrictions for CDC Replication. Before migrating data, evaluate the performance of the source and destination databases. Migrate data during off-peak hours. Otherwise, initial full data synchronization consumes read and write resources on the source and destination databases, which may increase the database load. Initial full data synchronization concurrently runs INSERT operations. This causes table fragmentation in the destination database. As a result, the tablespace of the destination instance is larger than that of the source instance after the initial full data synchronization is complete. During the DTS migration, if data from sources other than DTS is written to the destination database, data inconsistency may occur between the source and destination databases. |

| Special cases | Because the source Db2 for LUW database is a self-managed database, note the following: During migration, if a primary/standby switchover occurs on the source database, the migration task fails. The latency of DTS is calculated based on the difference between the timestamp of the last migrated data entry in the destination database and the current timestamp. If no DML operations are performed on the source database for a long time, the latency information may be inaccurate. If the latency displayed for the task is too high, perform a DML operation on the source database to update the latency information. Note If you choose to migrate the entire database, you can also create a heartbeat table. Data is updated or written to the heartbeat table every second. |
|---|---|

**SQL operations supported by incremental migration**

| Operation type | SQL statement |
|---|---|
| DML | INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE |

**Preparations**

Create an account and grant permissions The Db2 for LUW account must have the DBADM permission. The account for the PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance must be the owner of the destination schema for the migration objects. Enable archived logs for the Db2 for LUW database.

**Procedure**

1. Create a data migration instance.
When you create the instance, set **Source Database Type** to **DB2 LUW** and
**Destination Database Type** to **PolarDB for PostgreSQL**.
2. On the Data Migration page, find the data migration instance that you created, and click
**Configure Task** in the Actions column.
3. Configure the source and destination databases.

| Category | Configuration | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Task Name | None | The task name that DTS automatically generates. We recommend that you specify a descriptive name that makes it easy to identify the task. You do not need to specify a unique task name. |

| Source Database Information | Database Type | Fixed as DB2 LUW. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Connection Type | Select Public IP. |
|   | Instance Region | The region of the source instance that you selected when you purchased the data migration instance. This parameter cannot be changed. |
|   | DNS Or IP Address | Enter the IP address of the server that hosts the self- managed Db2 for LUW database. |
|   | Port | Enter the service port of the self-managed Db2 for LUW database. |
|   | Database Name | Enter the name of the database to which the tables to be migrated belong. |
|   | Database Account | Enter the database account of the self-managed Db2 for LUW database. |
|   | Database Password | Enter the password that corresponds to the database account. |
| Destination Database Information | Database Type | Select PolarDB for PostgreSQL. |
|   | Connection Type | Select Cloud Instance. |
|   | Instance Region | The region of the destination instance that you selected when you purchased the data migration instance. This parameter cannot be changed. |
|   | Architecture | In this example, Dual-node With Local Disks is selected. |
|   | PolarDB Instance ID | Select the ID of the destination PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance. |
|   | Database Name | Enter the name of the database that is created in the destination PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance to receive the migrated data. |
|   | Database Account | Enter the database account of the destination PolarDB for PostgreSQL instance. |

|   | Database Password | Enter the password of the database account. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Connection Method | Select a method as needed. |

4. After you complete the configuration, click **Test Connection And Proceed** at the bottom
of the page. If your self-managed Db2 for LUW database uses a whitelist, add the DTS server IP addresses from the dialog box to the whitelist. Then, click **Test Connection**
**And Proceed**.
If your self-managed Db2 for LUW database does not require a whitelist, click
**Test Connection And Proceed**.
5. Configure the task objects.

| Configu ration | Description |
|---|---|
| Task Steps | To perform only full data migration, select Schema Migration and Full Data Migration. To ensure service continuity during data migration, select Schema Migration, Full Data Migration, and Incremental Data Migration. Note If Incremental Data Migration is not selected, do not write data to the source database during full data migration. This ensures data consistency between the source and destination databases. |
| Process ing Mode For Existin g Tables In Destina tion | Precheck And Report An Error: Checks whether a table with the same name exists in the destination database. If no table with the same name exists, the precheck is passed. If a table with the same name exists, an error is reported during the precheck and the data migration task does not start. Ignore And Continue: Skips the check for tables with the same name in the destination database. Warning If you select Ignore And Continue, data inconsistency may occur and pose risks to your business. Examples: If the table schemas are the same and a record in the destination database has the same primary key value as a record in the source database, the record in the destination database is retained. The record from the source database is not migrated. If the table schemas are different, only data from some columns may be migrated, or the migration may fail. |

| Case- sensitiv ity Of Object Names In Destina tion Databa se | You can configure the case-sensitivity policy for the names of databases, tables, and columns of the migration objects in the destination instance. By default, DTS Default Policy is selected. You can also select a policy that is consistent with the default policy of the source or destination database. For more information, see Case-sensitivity of object names in the destination database. |
|---|---|
| Source Objects | Select one or more objects from the Source Objects section and click the icon to add the objects to the Selected Objects section. Note As needed, you can expand the navigation tree and use regular expressions to search for objects. You can select objects to migrate at the schema or table level. |
| Selecte d Objects | By default, after an object is migrated to the destination database, the name of the object remains unchanged. You can use the object name mapping feature to change the names of the objects that are migrated to the destination database. For more information, see Object name mapping. Note To filter data using a WHERE clause, right-click the table to be migrated in the Selected Objects section and set the filter condition in the dialog box that appears. To select the SQL operations performed on a specific database or table, right-click an object in the Selected Objects section. In the dialog box that appears, select the SQL operations that you want to migrate. If you use the object name mapping feature to rename an object, other objects that are dependent on the object may fail to be migrated. |

6. Click **Next: Advanced Configurations**.

| Configuration Item | Description |
|---|---|

| Retry Time After Connection To Source Or Destination Database Fails | After the migration task starts, DTS reports an error if the connection to the source or destination database fails. For predictable errors, DTS immediately and continuously retries the connection. The default retry period is 720 minutes. You can also specify a custom retry period in the range of 10 to 1,440 minutes. We recommend that you set the retry period to more than 30 minutes. If DTS reconnects to the source or destination database within the specified period, the migration task automatically resumes. Otherwise, the migration task fails. Note If you have multiple DTS instances, such as DTS instance A and DTS instance B, that share the same source or destination, and you set the network retry period to 30 minutes for instance A and 60 minutes for instance B, the shorter period of 30 minutes is used for both. |
|---|---|

7. In the lower part of the page, click **Next: Precheck and Start Task**.

**Important**

Before you can start the data migration task, DTS performs a precheck. You can start the data migration task only after the task passes the precheck. If the task fails to pass the precheck, click **View Details** next to each failed item. After you troubleshoot the issues based on the causes, run a precheck again.
8. Wait until **Success Rate** reaches 100%. Then, click **Back**.
If Incremental Data Migration is not selected, wait until the migration task is complete. If Incremental Data Migration is selected, the migration task does not automatically stop. In this case, you must wait until the migration task enters the **Running** state and is not delayed, and then manually stop the task.

#### 3.4.25 Migrate data between self-managed Redis databases

**Redis databases**

This topic describes how to migrate data between self-managed Redis databases by using Data Transmission Service (DTS).

**Prerequisites**

The version of the source Redis database is 2.8, 3.0, 3.2, 4.0, or 5.0. The source Redis database uses the standalone architecture rather than the cluster architecture. The `PSYNC` or `SYNC` command can be executed on the source Redis database.

**Limits**

| Category | Description |
|---|---|

| Limits on the source database | Bandwidth requirements: The server on which the source database is deployed must have sufficient outbound bandwidth. Otherwise, the data migration speed decreases. You must enable the data logging and append-only file (AOF) logging features for the source database. The database version of the source ApsaraDB for Redis instance cannot be 2.8. Limits on operations: If you perform only full data migration, do not write data to the source database during data migration. Otherwise, data may be inconsistent between the source and destination databases. To ensure data consistency, we recommend that you select full data migration and incremental data migration as the migration types. Limits on data migration from a standalone Redis database to a Redis database deployed in the cluster architecture: Each command can be run only on a single slot in a Redis database deployed in the cluster architecture. If you perform operations on multiple keys in the source database and the keys belong to different slots, the following error occurs: CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot We recommend that you perform operations on only one key during data migration. Otherwise, the migration task is interrupted. To ensure the stability of data migration, DTS inserts a key prefixed with DTS REDIS TIMESTAMP HEARTBEAT into the source database to record when data is _ _ _ updated. The key is filtered out during data migration. After the data migration task is complete, the key expires. If the source database is a read-only database or the source database account that is used to run the data migration task does not have the permissions to run the SETEX command, the reported latency may be inaccurate. To ensure the stability of data migration, we recommend that you increase the value of the repl-backlog-size parameter in the redis.conf file. |
|---|---|

| Other limits | If the data eviction policy maxmemory-policy of the destination database is not set to noeviction , data inconsistency may occur between the source and destination databases. If you run the EVAL or EVALSHA command to call Lua scripts, DTS cannot identify whether these Lua scripts are executed in the destination database. This is because the destination database does not explicitly return the execution results of Lua scripts during incremental data migration. When you run the PSYNC or SYNC command to transfer data of the LIST type, DTS does not perform the FLUSH operation on the existing data in the destination database. As a result, the destination database may contain duplicate data records. If an expiration policy is enabled for specific keys in the source database, these keys may not be deleted at the earliest opportunity after they expire. Therefore, the number of keys in the destination database may be less than that in the source database. You can run the INFO command to view the number of keys in the destination database. Note The number of keys that do not have the expiration policy enabled or have not expired is the same between the source and destination databases. To ensure compatibility, the version of the destination Redis database must be the same as or later than the version of the source Redis database. Before you migrate data, evaluate the impact of data migration on the performance of the source and destination databases. We recommend that you migrate data during off-peak hours. During full data migration, DTS uses the read and write resources of the source and destination databases. This may increase the loads on the database servers. During full data migration, concurrent INSERT operations cause fragmentation in the tables of the destination database. After full data migration is complete, the size of used tablespace of the destination database is larger than that of the source database. Make sure that the precision settings for columns of the FLOAT or DOUBLE data type meet your business requirements. DTS uses the ROUND(COLUMN,PRECISION) function to retrieve values from columns of the FLOAT or DOUBLE data type. If you do not specify a precision, DTS sets the precision for columns of the FLOAT data type to 38 digits and the precision for columns of the DOUBLE data type to 308 digits. DTS attempts to resume data migration tasks that failed within the last seven days. Before you switch workloads to the destination instance, stop or release the data migration task. You can also execute the REVOKE statement to revoke the write permissions from the accounts that are used by DTS to access the destination instance. Otherwise, the data in the source database overwrites the data in the destination database after the failed task is resumed. |
|---|---|
| Special cases | If you perform a primary/secondary switchover on the source or destination self- managed Redis database when the data migration task is running, the task fails. |

**Migration types**

Full data migration: DTS migrates the existing data of objects from the source database to the destination database. Incremental data migration: After full data migration is complete, DTS migrates incremental data from the source database to the destination database in real time.

**Commands that can be incrementally migrated**

APPEND BITOP, BLPOP, BRPOP, and BRPOPLPUSH DECR, DECRBY, and DEL EVAL, EVALSHA, EXEC, EXPIRE, and EXPIREAT FLUSHALL and FLUSHDB GEOADD and GETSET HDEL, HINCRBY, HINCRBYFLOAT, HMSET, HSET, and HSETNX INCR, INCRBY, and INCRBYFLOAT LINSERT, LPOP, LPUSH, LPUSHX, LREM, LSET, and LTRIM MOVE, MSET, MSETNX, and MULTI PERSIST, PEXPIRE, PEXPIREAT, PFADD, PFMERGE, PSETEX, and PUBLISH RENAME, RENAMENX, RESTORE, RPOP, RPOPLPUSH, RPUSH, and RPUSHX SADD, SDIFFSTORE, SELECT, SET, SETBIT, SETEX, SETNX, SETRANGE, SINTERSTORE, SMOVE, SPOP, SREM, and SUNIONSTORE ZADD, ZINCRBY, ZINTERSTORE, ZREM, ZREMRANGEBYLEX, ZUNIONSTORE, ZREMRANGEBYRANK, and ZREMRANGEBYSCORE

**Before you begin**

To ensure that incremental data migration tasks run as expected, we recommend that you remove the limit on the replication output buffer for the source database. In this topic, a server that runs on Linux is used in the example. If you perform only full data migration, skip the following steps.
1. Use the redis-cli program to connect to the source database.
You can use the redis-cli program after you install the Redis client. For more information, see Redis community official website.

```
redis-cli -h <host> -p <port> -a <password>
```

<host>: the endpoint that is used to connect to the source database. You can use 127.0.0.1 in this example. <port>: the service port number of the source database. The default port number is 6379. <password>: the password of the source database. Example:

```
redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6379 -a Test123456
```

2. Run the following command to remove the limit on the replication output buffer:

```
config set client-output-buffer-limit 'slave 0 0 0'
```

**Procedure**

1. Create a data migration instance.
2. On the Data Migration page, find the data migration instance that you created, and click
**Configure Task** in the Actions column.
3. Configure the source and destination databases. The following table describes the
parameters.

| Section | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| N/A | Task Name | DTS automatically generates a task name. We recommend that you specify a descriptive name for easy identification. The name does not need to be unique. |
| Source Database | Database Type | The type of the source database. Select Redis. |
|   | Access Method | The access method of the source database. Select Public IP Address. |
|   | Instance Region | The region in which the source database resides. If the Access Method parameter is set to Public IP Address, you do not need to configure the Instance Region parameter. |
|   | Instance Mode | The value of this parameter is fixed to Standalone and cannot be changed to Cluster. |
|   | Hostname or IP Address | The endpoint that is used to connect to the source database. |
|   | Port Number | The service port number of the source database. Default value: 6379. |
|   | Database Password | The password of the source database. If password verification is disabled for the source database, you do not need to enter the password. If you use the default account, whose username is the same as the instance ID, you can enter only the password. If you use a custom account, specify the password in the <Custom account username>:<Password> format. Example: testaccount:Test1234. |

| Destinati on Database | Database Type | The type of the destination database. SelectR edis. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Access Method | The access method of the destination database. SelectP ublic IP Address. |
|   | Instance Region | The destination region that you selected on the buy page. You cannot change the value of this parameter. |
|   | Instance Mode | The value of this parameter is fixed to Standalone and cannot be changed to Cluster. |
|   | Hostname or IP Address | The endpoint that is used to connect to the destination database. |
|   | Port Number | The service port number of the destination database. Default value: 6379. |
|   | Database Password | The password of the destination database. If password verification is disabled for the destination database, you do not need to enter the password. If you use the default account, whose username is the same as the instance ID, you can enter only the password. If you use a custom account, specify the password in the <Custom account username>:<Password> format. Example: testaccount:Test1234. |

4. In the lower part of the page, click **Test Connectivity and Proceed**.
5. If a whitelist is configured for the self-managed Redis database, you must manually add the
CIDR blocks of DTS servers to the whitelist of the database. After you configure the whitelist, click **Test Connectivity and Proceed**. If you do not need to configure a whitelist for the self-managed Redis database, ignore the preceding settings and click **Test Connectivity and Proceed**.
6. Select the objects to be migrated and the migration types.

| Parame ter | Description |
|---|---|

| Task Stages | If you want to perform only full data migration, select Full Data Migration. To ensure service continuity during data migration, select Full Data Migration and Incremental Data Migration. Note If Incremental Data Migration is not selected, do not write data to the source database during full data migration. This ensures data consistency between the source and destination databases. |
|---|---|
| Process ing Mode of Conflict ing Tables | Precheck and Report Errors: checks whether the destination database contains tables that have the same names as tables in the source database. If the source and destination databases do not contain tables that have identical table names, the precheck is passed. Otherwise, an error is returned during the precheck, and the data migration task cannot be started. Ignore Errors and Proceed: skips the precheck for identical table names in the source and destination databases. Warning If you select Ignore Errors and Proceed, data inconsistency may occur, and your business may be exposed to potential risks. If the source and destination databases have the same schema, DTS does not migrate data records that have the same primary keys as data records in the destination database. If the source and destination databases have different schemas, only specific columns are migrated or the data migration task fails. |
| Source Objects | Select one or more objects from the Source Objects section and click the icon to add the objects to the Selected Objects section. Note You can select only databases as the objects to be migrated. You cannot select keys as the objects to be migrated. |
| Selecte d Objects | By default, after an object is migrated to the destination database, the name of the object remains unchanged. You can use the object name mapping feature to change the names of the objects that are migrated to the destination database. For more information, see Object name mapping. Note If you use the object name mapping feature to rename an object, other objects that are dependent on the object may fail to be migrated. |

7. Click **Next: Advanced Settings**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Retry Time for Failed Connection | The retry time range for failed connections. If the source or destination database fails to be connected after the data migration task is started, DTS immediately retries a connection within the retry time range. Valid values: 10 to 1440. Unit: minutes. Default value: 720. We recommend that you set the parameter to a value greater than 30. If DTS reconnects to the source and destination databases within the specified time range, DTS resumes the data migration task. Otherwise, the data migration task fails. Note If you set different retry time ranges for multiple data migration tasks that have the same source or destination database, the shortest retry time range that is set takes precedence. |
| Configure ETL | The extract, transform, and load (ETL) feature cannot be enabled for this data migration task. Select No. |

8. In the lower part of the page, click **Next: Precheck and Start Task**.

**Important**

Before you can start the data migration task, DTS performs a precheck. You can start the data migration task only after the task passes the precheck. If the task fails to pass the precheck, click **View Details** next to each failed item. After you troubleshoot the issues based on the causes, run a precheck again.
9. Wait until **Success Rate** reaches 100%. Then, click **Back**.
If Incremental Data Migration is not selected, wait until the migration task is complete. If Incremental Data Migration is selected, the migration task does not automatically stop. In this case, you must wait until the migration task enters the **Running** state and is not delayed, and then manually stop the task.

#### 3.4.26 Migrate data from an ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance to a self-managed Kafka cluster

**MongoDB instance to a self-managed Kafka**

**cluster**

Data Transmission Service (DTS) allows you to migrate data from an ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance to a self-managed Kafka cluster. This topic describes how to migrate data from an ApsaraDB for MongoDB replica set instance to a self-managed Kafka cluster.

**Prerequisites**

The destination Kafka cluster is created and the Kafka version is 0.10 to 2.7. A topic is created in the destination Kafka cluster to receive the migrated data. The endpoints of all shard nodes are obtained and the usernames and passwords of the accounts used to log in to the shard nodes are consistent if the source database is an ApsaraDB for MongoDB sharded cluster instance.

**Usage notes**

| Category | Description |
|---|---|

| Limits on the source database | The server on which the source database is deployed must have sufficient outbound bandwidth. Otherwise, the data migration speed decreases. If you select collections as the objects to be migrated and you want to modify the collections in the destination database, such as renaming the collections, you can migrate up to 1,000 collections in a single data migration task. If you run a task to migrate more than 1,000 collections, a request error occurs. In this case, we recommend that you configure multiple tasks to migrate the collections. If the source database is an ApsaraDB for MongoDB sharded cluster instance: The id field in the collection to be migrated must be unique. Otherwise, _ data inconsistency may occur. The number of mongos nodes in the source database cannot exceed 10. Make sure that the MongoDB balancer of the source database is disabled during full data migration. Do not enable the balancer until all full data migration is complete and incremental data migration starts. Otherwise, data inconsistency may occur. Make sure that orphaned documents are deleted in the destination ApsaraDB for MongoDB sharded cluster instance. Otherwise, data inconsistency may occur, or even the task may fail. Do not perform commands that change data distribution of the objects to be migrated in the source database when the migration task is in progress. Otherwise, data between the source and destination database may be inconsistent. Such commands include shardCollection, reshardCollection, unshardCollection, moveCollection, and movePrimary. The source database cannot be a standalone ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance. The operation logging feature must be enabled. Note If you perform only incremental data migration, the oplogs of the source database must be retained for more than 24 hours. If you perform both full data migration and incremental data migration, the oplogs of the source database must be retained for at least seven days. Otherwise, DTS may fail to obtain the oplogs and the task may fail. In exceptional circumstances, data inconsistency or loss may occur. After full data migration is complete, you can set the retention period to more than 24 hours. Make sure that you set the retention period of oplogs based on the preceding requirements. Otherwise, the Service Level Agreement (SLA) of DTS does not guarantee service reliability or performance. During full data migration, do not change the schemas of databases or collections. Otherwise, the data migration task fails. Schema changes include array updates. |
|---|---|

| Other limits | Schema migration is not supported. The service port of the Kafka cluster must be accessible over the Internet. Only collections can be migrated. DTS cannot migrate data from the admin, config, or local database. If a single data entry to be migrated exceeds 10 MB, the task fails. If the source database is an ApsaraDB for MongoDB sharded cluster instance: If the balancer of the source database balances data, the migration task may be delayed. DTS cannot guarantee the order in which different partitions in the source database are written to the destination Kafka database. Transaction information is not retained. When transactions are migrated to the destination database, the transactions are converted into single records. When the migration task is running, if the destination Kafka cluster is scaled out or in, such as adding or reducing Kafka broker nodes, you must restart the migration task. Make sure that DTS can connect to the source and destination databases. For example, the security settings of the database instance and the listeners and advertised.listeners parameters in the server.properties configuration file of the self-managed Kafka cluster do not restrict access to DTS. During full data migration, DTS consumes read and write resources of the source and destination databases. This may increase the loads of the database servers. Before you start the migration task, assess the impact of data migration on the performance of the source and destination databases. We recommend that you migrate data during off-peak hours, such as when the CPU usage of the source and destination databases is lower than 30%. DTS attempts to restore failed tasks within the last seven days. Before you switch your workloads to the destination database, stop or release the data migration task. Otherwise, the data in the source database overwrites the data in the destination database after the task is resumed. DTS calculates the latency of incremental data migration based on the timestamp of the latest migrated data in the destination database and the current timestamp in the source database. If no update operation is performed on the source database for an extended period of time, the migration latency may be inaccurate. If the latency of the data migration task is excessively high, you can perform an update operation on the source database to update the latency. |
|---|---|

**Migration types**

| Migration type | Description |
|---|---|
| Full data migration | All existing data is migrated from the source ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance to the destination Kafka cluster. Note DTS supports full data migration for the following types of objects: database and collection. |

| Incremental data migration | In addition to the existing data, incremental data on the source ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance is also migrated to the destination Kafka cluster. A DTS task does not migrate incremental data from databases that are created after the task starts. DTS migrates incremental data generated by the following operations: CREATE COLLECTION and CREATE INDEX DROP DATABASE, DROP COLLECTION, and DROP INDEX RENAME COLLECTION The operations that are performed to insert, update, or delete documents in a collection. |
|---|---|

**Procedure**

1. Create a data migration task.
When you create the data migration task, select **MongoDB** as the **source database**
**type** and **Kafka** as the **destination database type**.
2. On the Data Migration page, find the data migration task that you created and click
**Configure Task**.
3. Configure the source and destination databases.

| Section | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Task Name | N/A | The name of the task. DTS automatically generates a task name. We recommend that you specify an informative name to identify the task. You do not need to specify a unique task name. |
|   | Database Type | The type of the destination database. SelectM ongoDB. |
|   | Access Method | The access method of the destination database. SelectA libaba Cloud Instance. |
|   | Instance Region | The region in which the source PolarDB for PostgreSQL cluster resides. The region is the source region that you selected when you created the data migration task. You cannot change the value of this parameter. |
|   | Replicate Data Across Alibaba Cloud Accounts | Specifies whether to migrate data between instances that belong to different Alibaba Cloud accounts. Select No. |
|   | Architecture | The architecture of the source ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance. In this example, Replica Set is selected. |

| Source Database |   |   |
|---|---|---|
|   | Cluster ID | The ID of the source ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance. |
|   | Authenticati on Database | The name of the authentication database in which the database account is created. |
|   | Database Account | The account of the source database. The account must have the read permissions on the source database, admin database, and local database. |
|   | Database Password | The password of the database account. |
|   | Encryption | Specifies whether to encrypt the connection to the destination database. Select Non-encrypted or SSL-encrypted based on your business requirements. If you select SSL-encrypted, you must enable SSL encryption for the ApsaraDB for MongoDB instance before you configure the data migration task. Note This parameter is available and required only when Architecture is set to Replica Set. |
|   | Database Type | The type of the destination database. SelectK afka. |
|   | Access Method | The access method of the destination database. SelectP ublic IP Address. |
|   | Instance Region | The region in which the destination Kafka cluster resides. The region is the same as the destination region that you selected when you created the data migration task. You cannot change the value of this parameter. |
|   | Domain Name or IP | The IP address that is used to access the self-managed Kafka cluster. In this example, the public IP address is used. |
|   | Port Number | The service port number of the Kafka cluster. Default value: 9092. |
|   | Database Account | The username that is used to log in to the Kafka cluster. If no authentication is enabled for the Kafka cluster, you do not need to enter the username. |
|   | Database Password | The password of the username. If no authentication is enabled for the Kafka cluster, you do not need to enter the password. |

| Destination Database |   |   |
|---|---|---|
|   | Kafka Version | The version of the destination Kafka cluster. Note You cannot select a Kafka Version later than 1.0 in the console. If you are using a Kafka version later than 1.0, you must select Kafka 1.0. |
|   | Encryption | Specifies whether to encrypt the connection to the destination cluster. Select Non-encrypted or SCRAM-SHA-256 based on your business and security requirements. |
|   | Topic | The name of the destination topic. Select a value from the drop- down list. |
|   | Topic That Stores DDL Information | The topic that stores the DDL information. Select a topic from the drop-down list. If you do not set this parameter, the DDL information is stored in the topic that is specified by the Topic parameter. |
|   | Use Kafka Schema Registry | Specifies whether to use Kafka Schema Registry. Kafka Schema Registry provides a serving layer for your metadata. It provides a RESTful API to store and retrieve your Avro schemas. Valid values: No: does not use Kafka Schema Registry. Yes: uses Kafka Schema Registry. In this case, you must enter the URL or IP address that is registered in Kafka Schema Registry for your Avro schemas. |

4. In the lower part of the page, click **Test Connectivity and Proceed**.
If a whitelist is configured for your self-managed Kafka cluster, add the CIDR blocks of DTS servers that are displayed in the dialog box to the whitelist of the self-managed Kafka cluster. Then, click **Text Connectivity and Proceed**. If you do not need to configure a whitelist for your self-managed Kafka cluster, ignore the preceding settings and click **Test Connectivity and Proceed**.
5. Select the migration policy and the objects to be migrated. The following table describes
the parameters.

| Parame ter | Description |
|---|---|
| Task Stages | By default, Incremental Data Migration is selected. By default, you must also select Full Data Migration. Schema Migration is not supported. |

| Process ing Mode of Conflict ing Tables | Precheck and Report Errors: checks whether the destination database contains tables that use the same names as tables in the source database. If the source and destination databases do not contain tables that have identical table names, the precheck is passed. Otherwise, an error is returned during the precheck, and the data migration task cannot be started. Ignore Errors and Proceed: skips the precheck for identical table names in the source and destination databases. Warning If you select Ignore Errors and Proceed, data inconsistency may occur, and your business may be exposed to potential risks. If the source and destination databases have the same schemas, DTS does not migrate data records that have the same primary key values as data records in the destination database. If the source and destination databases have different table schemas, only specific columns are migrated, or the data migration task fails. |
|---|---|
| Data Format in Kafka | Only Canal Json is supported. Note For more information, see Canal Json. |
| Policy for Shippin g Data to Kafka Partitio ns | The policy based on which data is migrated to the Kafka cluster. Select a policy based on your business requirements. For more information, see Specify the policy for migrating data to Kafka partitions. |
| Capitali zation of Object Names in Destina tion Instanc e | The capitalization of database names, table names, and column names in the destination instance. By default, DTS default policy is selected. You can select other options to ensure that the capitalization of object names is consistent with that in the source or destination database. For more information, see Specify the capitalization of object names in the destination instance. |

| Source Objects | Select one or more objects in the Source Objects list and click the icon to add the objects to the Selected Objects list. Note You can use the navigation tree to search for one or more objects. You can select tables or databases as the objects to be migrated. |
|---|---|
| Selecte d Objects | By default, after an object is migrated to the destination database, the name of the object remains unchanged. You can use the object name mapping feature to rename the objects that are migrated to the destination database. For more information, see Object name mapping. Note If you use the object name mapping feature to rename an object, other objects that are dependent on the object may fail to be migrated. |

6. Click **Next: Advanced Settings** to configure advanced settings. The following table
describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Retry Time for Failed Connections | The retry time range for failed connections. If the connection to the source or destination database fails after the data migration task is started, an error is returned. For predictable errors, DTS immediately retries a connection within the time range. Valid values: 10 to 1440. Unit: minutes. Default value: 720. We recommend that you set the parameter to a value greater than 30. If DTS reconnects to the source and destination databases within the specified retry time range, DTS resumes the data migration task. Otherwise, the migration task fails. Note If you set different retry time ranges for multiple data migration tasks that have the same source or destination database, the shortest retry time range that is set takes precedence. |

7. In the lower part of the page, click **Next: Precheck and Start Task**.

**Important**

Before you can start the data migration task, a precheck is performed. You can start the data migration task only after the task passes the precheck. If the task fails to pass the precheck, click **View Details** next to each failed item. After you troubleshoot the issues based on the causes, run a precheck again.
8. Wait until **Success Rate** reaches 100% and then click **Back**.
If Incremental Data Migration is not selected, wait until the migration task is complete. If Incremental Data Migration is selected, the migration task does not automatically stop. In this case, you must wait until the migration task enters the **Running** state and is not delayed, and then manually stop the task.

#### 3.4.27 Migrate data from a MaxCompute project to a MySQL database

**project to a MySQL database**

This topic describes how to migrate data from a MaxCompute project to a MySQL database by using Data Transmission Service (DTS). In this example, an ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance is used as the destination instance.

**Usage notes**

During a full data migration, DTS consumes read and write resources on the source and destination databases, increasing their load. If your databases have poor performance, low specifications, or high workloads (for example, if the source database has many slow SQL queries or tables without primary keys, or if deadlocks occur in the destination database), the increased load can strain your databases or even cause service interruptions. Perform the data migration during off-peak hours, such as when the CPU utilization of both databases is below 30%. DTS automatically creates a database in the destination ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance. However, if the name of the source database is invalid, you must manually create a database in the destination instance before you configure the data migration task. For more information about ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instances and how to create a database in an ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance, see the "Create a database" topic in the documentation of ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL. To ensure data consistency, we recommend that you do not write data to the source MaxCompute project during full data migration. If a data migration task fails, DTS automatically resumes the task. Before you switch your workloads to the destination instance, stop or release the data migration task. Otherwise, the data in the source database overwrites the data in the destination instance after the task is resumed. MaxCompute does not support the PRIMARY KEY constraint. If network errors occur, DTS retries the data migration task. In this case, duplicate data records may be migrated to the destination tables that do not have primary keys. DTS cannot migrate incremental data from a MaxCompute project to an ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance. To ensure data consistency, we recommend that you do not write data to the source MaxCompute project during data migration.

**Migration types**

| Migration type | Description |
|---|---|
| Schema migration | DTS migrates the schemas of the required objects to the destination database. DTS supports schema migration for views, tables, and databases. Warning In this topic, the source and destination databases are heterogeneous databases. The schemas of the source and destination databases may be inconsistent after schema migration. We recommend that you evaluate the impact of data type conversion on your business. For more information, see Data type mappings between heterogeneous databases. |
| Full data migration | DTS migrates full data of the required objects to the destination database. Note During full data migration, concurrent INSERT operations cause fragmentation in the tables of the destination database. After full data migration is complete, the used tablespace of the destination database is larger than that of the source database. |

**Procedure**

1. Create a data migration instance.
2. On the Data Migration page, find the data migration instance that you created, and click
**Configure Task** in the Actions column.
3. Configure the source and destination databases.

| Section | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| N/A | Task Name | The task name that DTS automatically generates. We recommend that you specify a descriptive name that makes it easy to identify the task. You do not need to specify a unique task name. |
| Source Database | Database Type | The type of the source database. Select MaxCompute. |
|   | Access Method | The access method of the destination database. SelectA libaba Cloud Instance. |
|   | Instance Region | The region of the source MaxCompute project. The region is the source region that you selected when you created the data migration task. You cannot change the value of this parameter. |
|   | Project | The name of the MaxCompute project. You can view the name of the MaxCompute project on the Projects page in the MaxCompute console. |

|   | accessKeyId | The AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret of the account that you use to connect to the destination ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance. Note For information about how to obtain the AccessKey ID, see the Obtain an AccessKey pair topic of the Developer Guide of MaxCompute. |
|---|---|---|
|   | accessSecre t |   |
| Destination Database | Database Type | The type of the source instance. Select MySQL. |
|   | Access Method | The access method of the destination database. SelectA libaba Cloud Instance. |
|   | Instance Region | The region in which the destination ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance resides. The region is the destination region that you selected when you created the data migration task. You cannot change the value of this parameter. |
|   | RDS Instance ID | The ID of the destination ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance. |
|   | Database Account | The database account of the destination ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance. The account must have read and write permissions on the destination database. |
|   | Database Password | The password of the database account. After you configure the destination database parameters, click Test Connectivity next to Database Password to verify whether the configured parameters are valid. |

4. In the lower part of the page, click **Test Connectivity and Proceed**.
5. In the message that appears, click **OK**. In this step, the permissions on the MaxCompute
project are granted to the account used by DTS to migrate data.
6. Select the migration types and the objects to be migrated.

| Parame ter | Description |
|---|---|

| Capitali zation of Object Names in Destina tion Instanc e | The capitalization of database names, table names, and column names in the destination instance. By default, the DTS default policy is selected. You can select other options to make sure that the capitalization of object names is consistent with that in the source or destination database. For more information, see Specify the capitalization of object names in the destination instance. |
|---|---|
| Source Objects | Select one or more objects from the Source Objects section and click the icon to add the objects to the Selected Objects section. Note You can select columns, tables, or databases as the objects to be migrated. |
| Selecte d Objects | By default, after an object is migrated to the destination database, the name of the object remains unchanged. You can use the object name mapping feature to change the names of the objects that are migrated to the destination database. For more information, see Object name mapping. Note If you use the object name mapping feature to rename an object, other objects that are dependent on the object may fail to be migrated. |

7. Click **Next: Advanced Settings** to configure advanced settings. The following table
describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Retry Time for Failed Connections | The retry time range for failed connections. If the source or destination database fails to be connected after the data migration task is started, an error is returned. For predictable errors, DTS immediately retries a connection within the time range. Valid values: 10 to 1440. Unit: minutes. Default value: 720. We recommend that you set the parameter to a value greater than 30. If DTS reconnects to the source and destination databases within the specified retry time range, DTS resumes the data migration task. Otherwise, the migration task fails. Note If you specify different retry time ranges for multiple data migration tasks that have the same source or destination database, the shortest retry time range that is specified takes precedence. |

| Configure ETL | The extract, transform, and load (ETL) feature cannot be enabled for this data migration task. Select No. |

8. In the lower part of the page, click **Next: Precheck and Start Task**.

**Important**
